clue.text: Issue returned by boy at the last moment

parts.note: Justin is a boy's name

indicators.note: returned asks for the word for issue to be written back to front

parts.note: to issue is to emit or send out

explanation.surface: A boy finally turns in a problem, or an issue of a magazine, at the eleventh hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a noun (a magazine number) but is the verb: to emit. 'returned' turns that word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe arriving or acting barely before a deadline expires.

clue.text: Left work in American sucker's tin lizzie

indicators.note: in puts the left-and-work letters inside the American word

parts.note: jay is old US slang for a gullible person, a sucker
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Left a job working on an American fool's old Ford.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin Lizzie was the nickname of the Ford Model T, hence any old car.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms mean a battered old car; the first is the Model T's nickname.

clue.text: Smart, agent snatching short sleep

indicators.note: snatching means the agent grabs and holds the sleep within

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a nap is a brief sleep

explanation.surface: A sharp agent grabs a quick nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy dressing is smart and stylish, a sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Maiden secured by one fairly good ball — never mind the others!

indicators.note: secured by means the maiden is held fast beside the letter for one, which precedes it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
all right means satisfactory, fairly good
the jack is the small target ball in bowls

explanation.surface: A cricket maiden over secured by one decent delivery, with selfish indifference to teammates.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored; in bowls the jack is the small target ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British idiom expressing selfish complacency about others' troubles.

clue.text: Listener participation show at RKO — dial free

indicators.note: free here means released from order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A phone-in show at the RKO studio, with the dial set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges ATRKODIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This is radio built on listeners phoning in to discuss topics, so a participation show.

clue.text: Mount enthralling solitary landscape painter

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the mount letters surround the word for solitary

parts.note: solitary means one, single

explanation.surface: A mountain captivates a lone landscape artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet, the French Impressionist, painted landscapes such as his water lilies and haystacks.

clue.text: Somewhat obscene material turning stomachs over

indicators.note: turning, completed by over after the noun, says the word for stomachs is flipped end to end

parts.note: tums is an informal word for stomachs; over is the second half of the phrasal verb turning ... over

explanation.surface: Mildly dirty content that makes people feel queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning ... over' reverses TUMS. 'Somewhat' qualifies the definition: smut is mildly indecent matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is mildly indecent talk or pictures, the low-grade end of obscenity.

clue.text: Guy, old, playing popular instrument

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are in action, moving about

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: An old fellow strumming a popular instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges OLD into DOL.
explanation.definitionFit: This stringed instrument is like a small lute, played with a plectrum.

clue.text: Go lower and lower

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a board game
down means lower, as in further down the hill

explanation.surface: Descend further and further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb but is the noun: a go is a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower volume or heat is to reduce it by adjusting a control.

clue.text: Puzzle about circles circulated after party

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters following the party word

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: circulated means moved round, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A puzzle about circles handed round after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulated' rearranges ABOUTCIRCLES.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a word puzzle in which the initial and final letters of answers spell two words.

clue.text: Monk astride large pack animal

indicators.note: astride places the monk right up against the letter for large, sitting beside it

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

explanation.surface: A monk sits astride a big beast of burden.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American camelid is kept chiefly to carry loads, a classic beast of burden.

clue.text: Laird, perhaps, in an unhappy mood by end of tribunal

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of tribunal

parts.note: a downer is a spell of depression or gloom

explanation.surface: A Scottish laird sits glumly at the close of a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just sets the pieces side by side; the final L of 'tribunal' leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish estate owner, one example of a property holder, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Well-liked university in London area

indicators.note: in places the university letter within the London district

parts.note: Poplar is a district of east London

explanation.surface: A university in London that people are fond of.
explanation.walkthrough: POPLAR is a district in London's East End; U goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone popular is liked by many people, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Bad lot, I suspect, in newspaper

indicators.note: suspect, as an adjective meaning dubious or unreliable, tells us the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A rogue is suspected in a news report, as a crime story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges BADLOTI.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact-format popular paper, often sensational, is called this.

clue.text: What a crane may get, and what one may get from a crane?

definitions.text: What a crane may get, and what one may get from a crane?

parts.words: What a crane may get, and what one may get from a crane?
parts.note: a crane is both a long-legged wading bird, whose eye gives its own outlook, and a lifting machine high above the ground

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a crane gets, and what one gets from a crane.
explanation.walkthrough: The first crane is the bird, seeing through its own eye; the second is the tall machine, giving a view from on high.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a view from high above, as a flying creature would see the ground.

clue.text: Seriously ahead of time parked outside home

indicators.note: parked outside means the first word is placed around the second

parts.note: early means before the due time
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: Someone earnestly parked outside their home ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with sincere conviction is acting seriously, a synonym.

clue.text: Remove a bishop's booklet

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, plus S for the possessive
a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: Take away a bishop's pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop's' gives B'S, with the possessive S kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract is to extract or take away something, a formal verb sense.

clue.text: Passing across note, Calvin ordered something to drink in a Parisian bar

definitions.text: something to drink in a Parisian bar

indicators.note: passing across means the rearranged letters stretch over and round the note
ordered means put in a new arrangement

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is a written note

explanation.surface: Calvin passes a note across the bar and orders a drink in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges the name into VILANC; 'note' is NB (nota bene), which that stretch passes across.
explanation.definitionFit: White wine in French, the standard order in a Parisian café.

clue.text: Book full of promise about Cochran's style of music?

parts.note: bright prospects are promising ones
on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject
Eddie Cochran was an American rock and roll singer

explanation.surface: A book full of hope about a musician's style.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddie Cochran was a 1950s rock 'n' roll star. 'Book' is the definition: Graham Greene's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene's 1938 novel bears this title, named after the seaside sweet sold in that resort.

clue.text: Domineering female artist in Spanish port

indicators.note: in places the artist within the port

parts.note: Vigo is a port in Galicia, Spain
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A bossy woman artist living in a Spanish port.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew or harridan is a domineering woman, the word's main meaning.

clue.text: Characters immersed in scandal lied, as well as the rest

indicators.note: characters, meaning letters, sunk within the next words, say the answer lies among them

explanation.surface: People in a scandal lied, and the rest of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters immersed in' picks letters from 'scandal lied'.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal tag meaning plus everything else, added to the end of a list.

clue.text: Boyfriend, initially visiting model prison, brings pot

indicators.note: visiting puts the initial letter inside the word for model, as a guest goes in

parts.note: a toy is a model, as in a toy car

indicators.note: initially selects the first letter of Boyfriend

parts.note: jug is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A boyfriend visits his partner in jail and brings a pot along.
explanation.walkthrough: TO(B)Y then JUG; 'brings' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a pottery mug or jug shaped as a seated man in a tricorn hat, so a kind of pot.

clue.text: Cook taking breather round middle of afternoon

indicators.note: round says the breathing organ goes around the letter

parts.note: a gill is a fish's breathing organ

indicators.note: middle of picks the centre letter of afternoon

explanation.surface: A chef takes a break around mid-afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' suggests a rest, but it is GILL, the organ a fish breathes with.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill is to cook under direct heat, one cooking method.

clue.text: Feeling demonstrated by symbol Charlie left out

indicators.note: left out says one letter is dropped from the word for symbol

parts.note: an emoticon is a typed symbol such as a smiley face
Charlie is the NATO alphabet word for C

explanation.surface: An emotion shown by a symbol, with someone called Charlie excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' drops C from EMOTICON.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling such as joy or anger is a state of mind, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Revolutionary tsar China crushed

indicators.note: crushed suggests the letters of the two words are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A revolutionary crushes Russia's tsar, as in 1917.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' rearranges TSARCHINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wanting to overthrow all government is a type of revolutionary.

clue.text: Crown I found inside O'Hara's plantation

indicators.note: found inside places the letter I within the plantation name

parts.note: Tara is Scarlett O'Hara's family plantation in Gone with the Wind

explanation.surface: A crown discovered hidden at Scarlett O'Hara's home.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside TARA, the plantation in Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled headdress, a small crown worn on formal occasions.

clue.text: Changed course, reportedly, showing diplomacy

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so we want a word that sounds like the sailing term

parts.note: a sailing boat that tacked changed course into the wind

explanation.surface: Someone changed course, it was reported, showing diplomatic skill.
explanation.walkthrough: TACKED, a sailing term, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensitivity in dealing with others is the core meaning of diplomacy in everyday use.

clue.text: Old TV show for children produced by drama group

parts.note: a play is a drama
a school is a group, as of fish or of artists

explanation.surface: An old children's programme made by a theatre company.
explanation.walkthrough: Play School was a long-running BBC programme for young children.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the BBC's pre-school television programme from 1964 to 1988.
